notes: Blocked on this check: consumerfinance.gov (CFPB), cdc.gov, ready.gov, foodsafety.gov and fsis.usda.gov returned 403 to automated reads, so nothing was taken from them. consumer.ftc.gov and ftc.gov returned 404. Not worked round; a person can open them in a browser and add links later. The National Center for Home Food Preservation (nchfp.uga.edu) opened, but its footer says all rights reserved (University of Georgia), so it is link only. Everything on old canning, preserving and 'wholesome food' in the old books is unsafe by today's rules; always check against a current USDA source before teaching it.

courses.name: Why we eat what we eat
courses.why: Everyone eats three times a day and is a target of food marketing; knowing the biology, habits and politics helps a person choose and shop with open eyes.
units: What counts as food, and who decides
Hunger, taste and the body's hard wiring
Comfort, friends and eating as ritual
The modern food environment and why it nudges us
Cheap food, poverty and who can afford what
Labels, claims and what to ignore
Farming, organic and engineered food: the argument in plain words

courses.name: Kitchen science
courses.why: Knowing why bread rises and meat browns turns recipes from magic into skills a person can fix and invent with.
units: Old kitchen books versus modern science

courses.name: The old kitchen

units: Preserving then and now: what is unsafe today

courses.name: Is your food safe and honest
courses.why: From 1820 to today, people have been cheated by what is sold as food; spotting it protects health and money.
